prediction:
Take the bordered texture length from the shape the DECODER reads. Both arms run 5 times on the same disc (5-suites:392c13e5) so ab_compare measures the run-to-run band per capture instead of assuming it -- 2D_BorderTex_SZ is the flakiest capture in the corpus and a single-run delta on it is a coin flip.

THE MECHANISM, MEASURED FIRST. Arm A's own probe (dispatch 1789300529) printed decoded/tracked per distinct bordered shape: 4 for the 2D sizes with w,h >= 8, 256 for a bordered 1x1, 32 for 16x1, 1024 for a bordered 1x1x4 volume, and for a bordered cubemap the tracked range reaches 1.50 of six faces at 32x32 and 0.75 of ONE face at 4x4. It also counted blind=2 -- two bordered binds that declined to re-upload while the decoded range had changed since their last upload, both through the hash gate -- and border_swatch_origin.py independently named the two wrong swatches in that same run as pass-2 4x4 and pass-2 8x8, which are the two shapes the counter fired on (tracked=64 and tracked=256). For those sizes the tracked range is the top-left 4x4 or 8x8 texels of a 16x16 bordered surface, all of it the grey padding checkerboard that GenerateBordered2DSurface writes identically every iteration, so the hash cannot see a rewrite.

LEG 1 -- MUST NOT MOVE, and it is where the risk actually is. 94 captures, across Texture_cubemap, Volume_texture, TextureWrapMode, Texture_border_color, the nine 3D_BorderTex_SZ_*, the six Cube_BorderTex_SZ_* and xemu#1034, stay inside their measured band. Why they can move at all: the widened length feeds a TEST-AND-CLEAR dirty poll, so a bordered texture now consumes DIRTY_MEMORY_NV2A_TEX bits over 4 to 1,024 times more pages than before, and a range mark-and-clear that covers pages no consumer of this texture owns could hide a write from something else; it also widens download_surfaces_in_range_if_dirty and check_rt_as_texture_hazard, so more surface downloads and more hazard-detected barriers. The 3D and cube bordered captures are ON this list deliberately rather than excused: they are the shapes with the LARGEST shortfall, my model says they cannot move because each is one test with one bind and therefore no second bind to be blind on, and if one of them moves that model is wrong. FAILS in any world where the dirty-bit accounting or the surface overlap mattered to something I have not thought of.

LEG 2 -- THE SUBSTANTIVE ONE, and it is not a pixel count. Summed over the five runs of each arm, races_lost and stale_px from docs/testing/border_swatch_origin.py on Texture_border/2D_BorderTex_SZ must be strictly lower in arm B than in arm A. The model: a lost race at pass 1 currently ALSO costs the pass-2 swatch of the same size, because the pass-2 bind hits the same TextureKey, the truncated hash matches, and no re-upload happens. With the length fixed, pass 2 re-uploads. FAILS -- and this is a live world, not a formality -- if our pfifo lags a whole iteration consistently enough that the re-upload reads the successor again, in which case the inherited component is negligible and #44's skew is the whole story. That is the outcome that would send this to the pfifo rather than to texture.c, and the tool separates them: an inherited loss shows the successor's surface COMPLETE (arm A's pass-2 4x4 had cut=complete, wrong=1365), a loss to its own race shows a partial cut (arm A's pass-2 8x8 had cut=420). So the sharper form of this leg is that cut=complete on a pass-2 swatch should disappear, and any residual pass-2 loss should carry a partial cut.

LEG 3 -- LIVENESS, AND NOT A TAUTOLOGY OF THE CAPTURES. extra_upload > 0 in arm B's counters: at least one upload happened that the truncated hash would have suppressed. If this is zero the change did not fire and leg 2's result means nothing either way, which is exactly the confusion a flat capture count leaves behind. It is forced by my patch only in the sense that the patch is what makes the upload happen; what is NOT forced is that any such upload exists on this disc, which is a property of what the tests write.

LEG 4 -- NOT A FALSIFIER, stated so it is not counted: blind == 0 in arm B. Once the hashed range is the decoded range, a skip implies the decoded range was unchanged, so the truncated sub-range was too. My own change forces it. It is worth printing as a consistency check and worth nothing as evidence.

Texture_border/2D and Texture_border/2D_BorderTex_SZ are free to move, and are the only two. 2D_BorderTex_SZ is judged on stale_px and races_lost against the ten-run floor 0 0 0 0 0 146 181 1847 2352 2430 5640 (#44), never on differing pixels. NOTE on its status column: score_sweep flags it label-differs whenever a swatch goes stale, and that is a FALSE POSITIVE of the white-text heuristic -- measured on arm A, all 281 near-white mismatching pixels lie inside a swatch and none outside one, because the test's own kColors contains 0xFFFFFFFF and 0x66FFFFFF. The row is not void and must not be read as the goldens coming from a different build of the suite.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLAIM. It does not fix #44. The pass-1 race is untouched, and #44's own bar -- stale_px == 0 on 10 of 10 runs -- needs the pfifo skew bound. This removes the component that the length defect ADDS on top of it, and the five blind small swatches #44 records mean any loss count is still a lower bound.
notes: Both arms are queued with --runs 5 so ab_compare measures the per-capture band rather than assuming it. Arm A is a re-run of db7afd2076, the same ref as dispatch 1789300529, because that arm had runs=1 and a one-run baseline cannot supply a band for the one capture this change is about.

expect_counts is deliberately empty. The whole-arm better/worse count is the wrong criterion here: 2D_BorderTex_SZ is expected to move and is expected to move by a variable amount, so an exact count would have to be registered as either 'worse=1' or 'better=1' before knowing which way the flake fell. The criterion is must_not_move plus the stale_px/races_lost comparison in leg 2. This is the same mistake tex56-guard-inert.json made and it is not repeated.

Leg 2's quantities come from docs/testing/border_swatch_origin.py --json over both result directories, summed across the five runs of each arm. Its forward model reproduces all 73,728 golden swatch pixels exactly, which is what licenses naming which iteration a swatch rendered.
